title: Paprika (Capsicum annuum)
description: Precision greenhouse climate control and vegetative/generative crop steering for high-wire sweet peppers.
overview: Paprika (bell pepper) is a major high-tech greenhouse crop, typically trained in high-wire V-systems. Successful cultivation requires precise management of average daily temperature (ADT) and day/night temperature differentials (DIF) to maintain a balance between vegetative growth (stem and leaf size) and generative steering (fruit set and ripening). Unlike tomatoes, paprika has a distinct 'flushing' pattern where it sets fruit in cycles, requiring proactive steering adjustments.

climate_strategy.strategy: Predominantly grown in high-roof glasshouses and modern plastic houses. Focus is on maintaining strict night temperatures (18-19°C) during winter using heating pipes under gutters. VPD is managed actively to prevent blossom-end rot (BER) and sunscald. [1]
climate_strategy.tech_level: High (Gutter heating, automated vent screens, CO2 dosing)

climate_strategy.strategy: Utilizes high-wire V-systems allowing high density planting. Relies on advanced climate computers to steer crop load dynamically. High thermal screens and active dehumidification are used to maintain optimal VPD (0.8 - 1.2 kPa) and save energy.
climate_strategy.tech_level: Very High (Fully closed glasshouses, double screens, high-wire V-systems)

crop_steering.intro: Paprika steering focuses on avoiding excessive vegetative growth which leads to abortion of flower buds, while ensuring enough leaf canopy to prevent sunscald on ripening fruits.

vegetative_triggers.temperature_dif: Low day-to-night temperature difference (e.g., Day 21°C / Night 19°C) and warm ADT.
vegetative_triggers.vpd_target: 0.5 - 0.7 kPa (Ensures low transpiration stress, promoting leaf expansion).
vegetative_triggers.irrigation: Frequent, short irrigation shots starting early. Lower root-zone EC (2.0 - 2.2 mS/cm).

generative_triggers.temperature_dif: Large day-to-night temperature difference (e.g., Day 24°C / Night 16°C) to stimulate flowering.
generative_triggers.vpd_target: 0.9 - 1.2 kPa (Drives transpiration and calcium transport to fruits).
generative_triggers.irrigation: Larger dry-backs between shots. Higher root-zone EC (2.8 - 3.2 mS/cm) to limit vegetative stretch.

fertigation.intro: Paprika requires careful management of the Potassium-to-Nitrogen (K:N) ratio to steer vegetative/generative balance, and sufficient Calcium (Ca) to prevent blossom-end rot.
fertigation.vegetative_phase: Higher Nitrogen relative to Potassium. Target EC: 2.0 - 2.2 mS/cm. Keep pH in root zone between 5.5 - 6.2.
fertigation.generative_phase: Increase Potassium-to-Nitrogen ratio. Target EC: 2.5 - 3.0 mS/cm. Increase Calcium levels during high solar radiation days to support rapidly expanding fruits.

references.text: RDA (Rural Development Administration). Agricultural Technology Guide 124: Colored Sweet Pepper (Paprika) (2021 Rev.). Chapter 5 (Climate Control, p. 112-118).
references.publisher: Rural Development Administration, Republic of Korea
